title: Admissibility of the identity point morphism
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the identity compactification $s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s$. Then $a_s$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at every finite coefficient stage in the sense of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], with $c_{\mathrm{cd}}=0$ in [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] and $c_f^-=c_f^+=0$. The ambient compact-support functor and its right adjoint are naturally identified with the identity functor, with identity unit and counit. Under these identifications, the adjunction data agree under all compactification refinement comparisons. The finite-reduction and scalar-extension comparisons for these right adjoints are the identity transformations of the corresponding coefficient-change functors. The bounds are uniform in the coefficient stage, so the same morphism is admissible at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

proof.text: Construct beta_d with pointIdentitySupportIso from the proved section-normalized clopen theorem and exact precomposition of right derived functors. At all finite rings use the coefficient normalization equation of lem-sf-point-identity-support-normalization.
FullCD at the chosen proper identity compactification is zero by lem-sf-identity-full-cohomological-dimension, for every finite ring and all pro-etale base changes.

Define the actual ambient datum with right adjoints id and transported identity adjunctions. Set theta_r=beta_d followed by beta_e inverse, rho_r=id. Simplification of natural isomorphism identities proves the unit/counit and identity/composition equations, independently for every refinement. This is identityModel in Lean.

The normalized left coefficient equation implies its inverse composed with T(beta_A) equals beta_B. Expand mateEquiv for the transported identity adjunctions: cancellation gives that the canonical right coefficient map is identity. It is therefore invertible, even for nonflat reductions and equal exponents. These are identityModel_coefficient and identityModel_coefficient_isIso.

Identity preserves the constructible interval and finite Tor predicates definitionally, with both signed bounds zero. Assemble PointIdentityFiniteSystem at every finite extension and exponent. Use the same models for scalar maps. The defining finite-family criterion proves integral and rational admissibility. Shrink each finite intermediate subfield of the fixed algebraic closure, use the same models, and the field-inclusion algebra maps supply algebraically closed admissibility with uniform bounds 0,0,0. The finite field cardinality implies characteristic p, so ell distinct from p is a unit; map it through the Spec global-section isomorphism and germs to obtain hS.
